key_insight: A patient-specific digital twin plus explainable machine learning can map likely cardiac resynchronization therapy response across feasible coronary sinus pacing sites before the procedure.
clinical_relevance: This could help clinicians choose better left ventricular pacing sites, reduce non-response, and identify when alternative pacing strategies may be needed.
method: Built personalized 3D heart models from CT and LGE-MRI, including ventricular anatomy, fibrosis, and coronary sinus geometry.
Ran finite-element Eikonal simulations to estimate electrophysiologic features for candidate pacing sites.
Trained an explainable ML classifier on clinical variables plus model-derived indices, with SHAP used to show why each prediction was made.
evidence_signal: In 74 CRT candidates, the ML model outperformed a clinical calculator under leave-one-out cross-validation (accuracy 0.78 vs 0.58; AUC 0.78), and a pilot 19-patient coronary sinus cohort produced patient-specific response maps.
watch_item: This is a pilot framework that needs larger, prospective validation before routine clinical implementation, especially because anatomy reconstruction and model inputs may not be available or consistent everywhere.
paper_title: Personalized planning of cardiac resynchronization therapy through integration of coronary sinus geometry, clinical data, digital twins, and machine learning: visualization, stratification, and optimization
